title: Separate nonuniform TC⁰ from NC¹
formal: Is there a language in nonuniform NC¹ that is not in nonuniform TC⁰?
definitions: A language is a set of finite binary strings. A circuit family has one Boolean circuit for each input length n and need not be computably generated. NC¹ consists of languages computed by circuits with at most n^{O(1)} gates and depth O(log(n+2)), using fan-in-two AND and OR gates and unary NOT gates. TC⁰ allows unbounded-fan-in AND, OR and majority gates and NOT gates, with polynomial size and a depth bound independent of n. A majority gate outputs one when at least half its input bits are one. Input wires count toward the polynomial description size. Constants may depend on the language; there are no oracle gates. The known inclusion TC⁰⊆NC¹ makes the question a strictness problem.

context_blocks.text: Threshold circuits can aggregate many inputs in one layer, but a fixed number of layers may still be weaker than logarithmic-depth computation. This is one of the basic unresolved boundaries between standard Boolean circuit models.

The cited work quantifies how stronger bounds for threshold circuits would imply separations. Its conclusions are conditional implications, not a proof that NC¹ exceeds TC⁰. The existing NEXP-versus-TC⁰ card uses a much larger source class and asks a different separation.

why: Locate a central boundary in the expressive power of shallow threshold computation.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.

title: Tutte’s nowhere-zero 5-flow conjecture
formal: Does every finite bridgeless undirected multigraph admit an orientation and integer values f(e)∈{1,2,3,4} on its edges such that total incoming flow equals total outgoing flow at every vertex?
definitions: Parallel edges and loops are allowed; a loop contributes once to each side of the conservation equation. An edge is a bridge if deleting it increases the number of connected components. Isolated vertices and disconnected graphs are permitted. An orientation chooses a direction for each nonloop edge. All equalities are ordinary integer equalities, not only congruences modulo five. No efficiency requirement is imposed on the orientation or flow.

context_blocks.text: Nowhere-zero flows are a fundamental integral counterpart of graph coloring and circulation. The condition of having no bridges is necessary for a nonzero conserved flow and is the only hypothesis in Tutte’s conjecture.

Seymour proved that six suffices for every bridgeless graph. Reducing the universal bound to five is a longstanding structural threshold, with a broad graph-theoretic role beyond one algorithm. Signed graphs and vector-valued flows give related questions but are not this target.

why: Resolve a central universal threshold for integral graph flows, linking coloring and circulation structure.

title: Decidability of PL 4-sphere recognition
formal: Is there a Turing algorithm that, for every finite simplicial complex promised to triangulate a closed connected PL 4-manifold, halts and decides whether it is PL-homeomorphic to the boundary of a 5-simplex?
definitions: The input lists vertices and maximal 4-simplices, with all faces implicit. Its geometric realization is promised to be a compact connected PL 4-manifold without boundary. Two finite complexes are PL-homeomorphic when some finite subdivisions are simplicially isomorphic. The boundary of the 5-simplex fixes the standard PL structure on S⁴. No running-time bound is requested, and behavior outside the promise is unrestricted. Topological homeomorphism without preserving the PL category is a different target.

context_blocks.text: Four dimensions are a special boundary for algorithmic manifold topology. Even the existence of a recognition procedure for the standard PL sphere is unresolved in the cited discussion.

The formulation fixes the PL category, avoiding confusion with topological or smooth recognition. Higher-dimensional undecidability theorems cannot simply be transferred to dimension four. Conversely, recognizing a topological sphere would not alone establish that a supplied PL structure is standard.

why: Locate a foundational decidability boundary in computational topology.

title: Explicit binary codes attaining the Gilbert–Varshamov bound
formal: For every fixed δ∈(0,1/2), can binary codes of relative distance at least δ and asymptotic rate at least 1−H₂(δ) be constructed deterministically in polynomial time?
definitions: A binary block code maps distinct messages to distinct binary words of a common length n. Relative distance is the minimum Hamming distance divided by n; rate is log₂ of the number of messages divided by n. H₂ is binary entropy. Construction must give a succinct polynomial-time encoder rather than explicitly enumerate exponentially many codewords. No efficient decoder is required, and no improvement beyond the GV rate is requested.

context_blocks.text: Random binary codes attain the Gilbert–Varshamov tradeoff, but an efficient deterministic construction remains a central explicit-coding question. It asks for access to optimal known objects, not a stronger information-theoretic existence bound.

The coding materials explicitly separate attaining the bound constructively from beating it existentially. The inherited TCS-1012 has a list-decoding-capacity source and a misleading distance-bound title; it is not used as a duplicate for this minimum-distance construction.

why: Turn the basic random-code rate-distance guarantee into an efficiently usable explicit family.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.

title: Exponential parallel repetition for every two-player entangled game
formal: For every finite two-player one-round game G with ω*(G)<1, does a constant c_G>0 exist such that ω*(G^⊗k)≤exp(−c_G k) for every integer k≥1?
definitions: G consists of finite nonempty question and answer sets X,Y,A,B, a probability distribution μ on X×Y and a predicate V:X×Y×A×B→{0,1}. The players share an arbitrary finite-dimensional bipartite quantum state and, without communicating, answer their individual questions using local positive-operator-valued measurements. Such a measurement is a finite family of positive semidefinite operators summing to the identity; outcome probabilities obey the Born rule. ω* is the supremum of the winning probability over all finite dimensions, states and measurements. G^⊗k samples k independent question pairs; the players receive their entire question tuples and win only if every coordinate passes V. Their measurements may act jointly across coordinates. The constant may depend on the entire game, with no uniform rate across games required.

context_blocks.text: Parallel repetition is supposed to amplify the soundness of a verification game. Entangled strategies can correlate answers across repeated instances, making the amplification theorem substantially different from its classical counterpart.

The source develops parallel repetition for entangled games and identifies the general exponential-decay challenge. Later convergence-to-zero results and exponential theorems for restricted game classes do not prove this universal rate. The existing TCS-5077 concerns the weaker convergence question.

title: Wait-free queues from two-process consensus objects
formal: For every finite n≥2, can a linearizable unbounded FIFO queue with n unrestricted enqueuers and dequeuers be implemented deterministically and wait-free using atomic registers and two-process consensus objects?
definitions: A queue begins empty. Enqueue(v) appends a finite binary value; dequeue returns and removes the oldest remaining value, or returns EMPTY when none remains. Linearizability requires every finite concurrent history to extend to a sequential legal queue history consistent with the real-time order of nonoverlapping completed calls. Wait freedom requires each call by a process that continues taking steps to finish after finitely many of its own steps, regardless of delays or crashes elsewhere. A two-process consensus object accepts at most one proposal from each of two designated processes and returns one proposed value consistently to both; processes may use arbitrarily many objects and registers. No stronger primitive, randomization or bound on total queue length is supplied.

context_blocks.text: A queue has consensus number two, but that upper bound does not automatically give an implementation from consensus objects of the same level. The question tests the completeness of level two for a basic concurrent data structure.

Eisenstat implements a queue with only two possible enqueuers in Common2. General queues permit every process to enqueue and dequeue repeatedly, so that restriction does not settle the target. The process count may affect the implementation, which must support arbitrarily long histories.

why: Clarify the relation between synchronization power and implementability of a canonical concurrent object.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
